To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a class of voltage-gated membrane equations can be reduced in a systematic way to a mathematical mechanism that was previously analyzed by Er­ mentrout and Kopel in [7], and that the reduction is valid under the hypothesis that a slow periodic orbit must be close to a curve in the fast phase plane that contains degenerate homoc­ linic points.
the parabolic mechanism is a general phenomenon and that it can be reduced to a two-dimensional model with a fast variable and one slow variable.
parabolic bursting is a generic phenomenon for voltage-gated conductances, and that the mathematical model in [7] describes a wide class of voltage-gated systems.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following question: Under what conditions can a class of voltage-gated equations be reduced to the Ermentrout-Kopell mechanism?
the analysis and control of parabolic bursting in excitable membrane systems.
the mathematical analysis of a class of parabolic bursters and the development of a new theory for the reduction of voltage-gated systems to a simpler form.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

a voltage-gated conduct-ance system with two slow variables, a fast variable and a fast threshold, and with a fast periodic orbit, has the same bifurcations and normal forms in the slow variables as the parabolic burster in [7], provided the slow variables are chosen so that the slow periodic orbit is near the curve of degenerate homo-clinic points.
parabolic bursting is generic for voltage-gated systems with a single slow variable, a single fast variable, and a single fast threshold variable.
the parabolic mechanism in [7], which is a two-dimensional slow-fast system, is a universal description of the bursting mechanism in a large class of excitable systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a parabolic burster is a system with a slow periodic orbit that stays close to a homoclinic curve of the fast system during the active phase.

the mechanism of Ermentrout & Kopell [7] is valid for a wide range of conductance equations, including those with voltage-dependent inactivation and those with voltage-dependent capacitance, and that the key hypothesis for our work is that a slow periodic orbit must lie near a degenerate homoclnic orbit for the fast system.
the parabolic burster mechanism of [7] applies to a larger class of conductance systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a wide class of voltage-gated systems can be analyzed using the mechanism in [8] and the theory in [7], and the mechanism is robust to perturbations of the voltage-gated system that do not destroy the slow manifold.
a parabolic burster can be understood as the slow passage of a trajectory from a saddle to an unstable periodic orbit, followed by its slow passage back to the saddle.
parabolic bursters can be understood as the intersection of a fast periodic orbit with a slow curve of degenerate equilibria.
